input.request: A friend is sending me £5,000 today and I have to pass it straight on to a crypto exchange. How do I make sure it doesn’t get blocked or held up?

events.text: Hi, quick one. A friend of mine is sending me £5,000 later today. As soon as it lands I need to send it straight on to my account at a crypto exchange. How do I make sure it doesn’t get blocked or held up by your checks?

To be clear, it isn’t really my money — he can’t use his own bank for crypto, so I’m just passing it through and he’s giving me £300 for helping. He said if anyone asks I should say it’s a gift. Should I split it into smaller amounts so it doesn’t trigger anything? It has to be done by tonight.

summary: Owen Pritchard, an unverified customer on secure chat, asked how to stop a £5,000 transfer from a friend, to be passed straight on to a crypto exchange, from being held up by the bank's checks. He later said it isn't his money, that he'd be paid £300, that he was told to call it a gift, and asked whether to split it into smaller amounts. The desk tried to refuse, but none of its refusal rules fitted, so it escalated the case as a possible money mule or structuring concern; no payment has been made. A person still needs to review it for financial crime and give Owen a warning and the permitted route.
